note: Curated extracts/summaries of PUBLIC-DOMAIN U.S. government sources. Each 'file' is our curated text; 'url' is the authoritative primary source it is drawn from. Always verify against the linked official page. U.S. federal government works are not subject to copyright.

sources.title: IRS: Foreign Student Liability for Social Security and Medicare Taxes (FICA)
sources.summary: When F-1/J-1 students are exempt from Social Security and Medicare (FICA) taxes, how the exemption is tied to nonresident status, and that OPT/CPT wages are covered while the student is a nonresident alien.

sources.title: IRS Publication 519: Substantial Presence Test and the Exempt Individual Rule
sources.summary: How the Substantial Presence Test works, the 5-year exempt-individual rule for F/J/M/Q students, and why residency status drives which tax form you file (1040-NR vs 1040).

sources.title: IRS Form 8843: Statement for Exempt Individuals
sources.summary: Who must file Form 8843, that F-1/J-1 students must file it even with no income, and how it is filed (attached to a return or mailed alone).

sources.title: IRS Form 1042-S: Foreign Person's U.S. Source Income Subject to Withholding
sources.summary: What Form 1042-S reports (scholarships over tuition, treaty-exempt wages, other U.S.-source income), how it appears on a student's return, and its ~March 15 furnishing timing.

sources.title: DHS/SEVP: Reporting to Your School & Initial SEVIS Registration
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) / SEVP — Study in the States
sources.summary: What to do right after you arrive: report to your DSO and complete your school's check-in so your DSO can complete initial SEVIS registration (within 30 days of the I-20 start date); I-901 fee + U.S. address prerequisites; each school sets its own required check-in forms on its international office website.

sources.title: USCIS/SEVP: F-1 On-Campus Employment Rules
sources.publisher: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) / SEVP
sources.summary: The 20-hours-per-week limit while school is in session, full-time during breaks, what counts as on-campus employment, and that no separate EAD is required.

sources.title: USCIS/SEVP: Curricular Practical Training (CPT)
sources.publisher: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) / SEVP
sources.summary: What CPT is, the one-academic-year and DSO-authorization requirements, part-time vs full-time, and the rule that 12+ months of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility.

sources.title: USCIS/SEVP: Optional Practical Training (OPT)
sources.publisher: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) / SEVP
sources.summary: 12 months of OPT per education level, pre- vs post-completion rules, applying via Form I-765 for an EAD, and the 90-day unemployment limit on post-completion OPT.

sources.title: USCIS/SEVP: STEM OPT 24-Month Extension
sources.publisher: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) / SEVP
sources.summary: The 24-month STEM OPT extension: E-Verify employer and Form I-983 requirements, filing via Form I-765, the 180-day pending-application work rule, and the extra 60 days (150 total) of unemployment.

sources.title: UIUC: International Student Check-In (ISSS)
sources.publisher: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign — International Student & Scholar Services (ISSS)
sources.summary: UIUC's mandatory new-student immigration check-in: the two-step ISSS process (online check-in form + in-person document review), documents to bring, and how it completes initial SEVIS registration. School-specific source shown only to UIUC students.

sources.title: CFPB: Sending Money Abroad — Remittance Transfer Protections
sources.summary: Consumer protections for sending money abroad: prepayment disclosures (exchange rate, fees, amount received), the ~30-minute cancellation right, and 180-day error-resolution rights.
